title: D&O insurance: what directors and managers should check
excerpt: Preparing a directors' liability assessment in Moldova: mandates, group structure, claims, defence costs and the conditions of a potential D&O policy.
imageAlt: Company directors reviewing documents on management mandates and business decisions

seo.title: D&O insurance in Moldova: a directors' checklist | ING Broker
seo.description: Check insured roles, group entities, periods, notification and defence costs before comparing directors' and officers' liability insurance prices.
seo.keywords: D&O insurance Moldova, directors liability insurance, officers liability, management mandates, defence costs

author: ING Broker editorial team
content:
D&O insurance concerns the liability of people managing a company, within the contract's limits. It should not be confused with company property insurance or professional liability for services delivered to customers. For a business in Moldova, the first question is whether an eligible solution exists for its entity, managers and jurisdictions.

What to clarify before comparing prices

A proposal labelled “D&O” does not by itself establish who is protected. Ask for the insured functions, group companies and circumstances in which the company itself is included. For a business in the Republic of Moldova, these points must be checked in the proposal and the conditions of the insurer assessing the risk.

  • Which people and mandates are included, including former directors and roles in subsidiaries?
  • Which date and notification trigger consideration of a claim?
  • Do defence costs reduce the total limit? Who approves the lawyer and expenditure?
  • How are known circumstances, investigations and changes of company control treated?
  • Which territories and courts are accepted?

Documents for an initial discussion

Prepare the group structure, business activities, countries of operation, financial statements and management role descriptions. Existing disputes or known circumstances should be discussed through a confidential channel. Do not send sensitive legal documents using a public enquiry form.

A record of management roles and terms of office

For each role being considered, prepare a record showing the entity, position, period and main activities. Separate a mandate in the person's own company from representation in a subsidiary or external organisation. Identify any separate service agreement. The record does not establish policy rights; it prevents a role being omitted because the description is too general.

Update this record when the mandate changes, not only at annual renewal. When someone leaves, retain information about the previous period in confidential company records. A first enquiry may require only role descriptions, with necessary personal details agreed later. Do not send identity document copies without a justified requirement and suitable channel.

A price question should not conceal a difference in scope

If one option appears cheaper, first check that the same group structure and mandates were assessed. A response prepared for a single entity is not automatically comparable with one covering a group. Ask for a summary of differences and information still requested. Keep the estimated cost separate from the final proposal. Where documentation is absent, mark the point unconfirmed rather than treating silence as promised cover.

The director, company and professional service are different roles

In a consultancy, the same person may manage the company and provide services to clients. A complaint about delivered work and a claim concerning a management decision should not be described as the same risk. The preparation file should explain the capacity in which each decision was made. A job title on a business card does not describe every activity.

For directors' and officers' liability insurance, start with the actual management structure. Record functions, entities and terms of office. If a director represents the firm in another company, show this separately. Do not assume every group position is included because one parent company exists. Proposed conditions should identify the people and situations being assessed.

How to prepare a company map for D&O assessment

A useful map can fit on one page. Place the applicant company in the centre, surrounded by subsidiaries, investments and countries with relevant activities. For each entity, state its business and relationship to the applicant. Separate active companies from those closing or reorganising. Do not reconstruct the structure from memory when current documents exist.

  • Use exact legal names, not only trading brands.
  • Identify recent ownership or management changes.
  • Show executive and supervisory functions that need discussing.
  • Describe activities in other jurisdictions without automatically applying foreign rules to Moldova.
  • Mark missing information and the person responsible for clarifying it.

Providing this map is preparation, not confirmation of eligibility. Where external finance, investors or major contracts are involved, add written insurance requirements. A generic questionnaire downloaded for another country does not prove the same conditions are available in the Republic of Moldova.

Preserve a claim timeline without improvised interpretations

Organise documents by date: the decision, relevant correspondence, when the company learned of a problem and notifications made. Separate documented facts from assumptions. An approximate date may change how a situation is understood, so check original messages and records. Do not retrospectively alter minutes to fit an insurance presentation.

Conditions may distinguish the period of the acts from when a claim is made or notified. Request an explanation of the actual proposal's mechanism. Do not infer protection merely because the policy is active on the day a complaint is read. This article sets no notification deadline and does not decide whether a particular claim is covered.

Who receives correspondence and forwards it?

Establish an internal route for documents addressed to management: the person registering them, the insurance contact and legal adviser. Keep delivery confirmations. The process should not depend entirely on a director's phone while they are on holiday. In a real situation, follow contractual conditions and specialist advice rather than waiting for the next renewal.

Compare the limit together with defence costs

Two proposals showing the same first-page limit may operate differently. Ask whether it is shared by several people, entities or claims and which expenditure reduces it. Distinguish defence costs, potential compensation and other named categories. A presentation figure should not be treated as a separate budget for every director.

Clarify lawyer selection and expenditure approval. If the company already has an adviser, check the procedure before assuming every fee will be accepted. Ask how the excess or deductible works, meaning the portion borne under the contract, and who pays it in the scenarios considered. Compare answers using the same working scenario rather than isolated marketing statements.

Renewal after management or ownership changes

Do not automatically copy last year's declarations. Review acquisitions, disposals, new activities, management changes and added jurisdictions. A company entering a new market may face a different situation even if its number of directors remains unchanged. Keep a list of differences and present it during assessment.

Ask about former directors, completed terms of office and notifications received after a change. Removing a person's name from an organisation chart does not resolve every question about previous activities. If an additional period or extension is proposed, obtain its actual conditions, duration and price. This article establishes no universal contractual option.

Documents that should not be uploaded to a public form

Disputes, allegations, personal information and lawyer correspondence may contain sensitive material. Start with a general company and needs description. Before sending detailed files, agree the recipient, channel and necessary documents. Do not publish them in article comments or automatically send the complete file to every supplier approached.

Prepare a list of available documents rather than an undifferentiated file collection. Mark the version and date of financial statements and organisation charts. If more information is requested, check its relevance to the assessment. An orderly process protects confidentiality and identifies unresolved issues without promising acceptance of the risk.

A comparison example without invented figures

Imagine two proposals for the same company. The first names only the applicant, while the second also describes a subsidiary. Before comparing prices, check whether the assessed scope is identical. Then compare people, territories, periods, notification, exclusions and defence costs. This illustrates a method, not existing offers or an insurer's conditions.

Conclude with three columns: confirmed in documents, expressly excluded and still to clarify. An empty field does not mean protection. Ask the broker to explain differences, and obtain legal advice on a director's actual liability. ING Broker is an intermediary. The insurer decides a claim under the contract.

Keep document names and dates sufficiently clear for another authorised colleague to reconstruct the comparison without relying on a verbal account. This does not require copying the complete confidential corporate archive into a shared enquiry file.

Frequently asked questions about D&O

Will a new policy resolve an already known dispute?

Do not assume so. Request a written assessment of the timeline and applicable conditions. Simply buying a policy does not confirm acceptance of an existing case.

Does D&O replace legal advice?

No. Assessment of a director's duties and dispute strategy require legal advice. The policy must be reviewed separately for the expenditure and claims provided by the contract.

What exactly should I ask the broker for?

An eligibility check and comparison of the same functions, territories, limits and periods, with unconfirmed points marked explicitly. A price and product name alone are insufficient.
